summary: Farb, Kisin and Wolfson prove that mod p cohomology classes of a smooth proper complex variety survive restriction to every dense Zariski open, in dimension at least h^{0,i} for primes of unramified good reduction with i < p − 2 (Theorem 4). The proof passes through Breuil–Kisin and A_inf log prismatic cohomology: a torsion-freeness lemma for Frobenius modules of small height, the mod p de Rham and Kummer-étale comparisons, Deligne–Illusie and Cartier reduce the claim to injectivity of restriction on global log differentials. Combined with the characteristic-class method (affine Artin vanishing and transfer) this bounds p-essential dimension: Theorem 2, Brosnan's conjecture for abelian varieties when p ≥ g + 2, and p-incompressibility of mod p homology covers of varieties of maximal Albanese dimension (Theorem 1). A cohomology computation for generalized Heisenberg groups via F_p^×-weights, torus torsors over abelian varieties and their toric compactifications, a tubular-neighbourhood variant, and Pink's boundary charts of toroidal compactifications give p-incompressibility of principal p-congruence covers of Hermitian locally symmetric varieties with Q-rank equal to R-rank (Theorem 3). The atlas plans the prismatic comparisons, derived completion, Cartier theory, toric and toroidal constructions, Shimura data and étale foundations it uses; it lacks essential dimension and everything downstream (a new roadmap), the Heisenberg group cohomology (a ProfiniteCohomology Part II), Hodge-type integral boundary charts, Kisin's abelian-type lifting, Prasad–Rapinchuk, the Deligne–Illusie decomposition, logarithmic purity and the Albanese variety. Eighteen mistakes are recorded, including missing prime bounds in Proposition 3.2.7, Theorem 3.3.17 and Corollary 2.3.12, a false statement in Proposition 3.2.14, and two gaps in the analytic essential-dimension argument; the main theorems survive with the stated corrections.

items.name: Essential dimension of a finite map
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 and f : Y → X a finite map of C-varieties. ed(Y/X) is the least integer e for which there are a dense Zariski open V ⊂ X, a finite map Y' → Z of C-varieties with dim Z = e and a map V → Z with Y|_V ≅ V ×_Z Y' over V.
items.note: Classical notion (Buhler–Reichstein); no roadmap plans essential dimension. The G-equivariant formulation used in the proofs is [FKW21, 2.1.4], item on the equivalent formulation below.

items.name: p-essential dimension of a G-cover
items.statement: For a finite group G, a G-cover Y → U (a finite étale G-torsor over a C-variety U) and a prime p, ed(Y/U; p) is the least d for which there exist: a dense Zariski open V ⊂ U; a finite étale π : E → V with p ∤ deg π; a morphism f : E → Z of C-varieties with dim Z = d; and a G-cover Z̃ → Z with f*Z̃ ≅ Y ×_U E as G-covers of E.

items.name: p-incompressible cover
items.statement: A G-cover Y → X of an irreducible C-variety X is p-incompressible if ed(Y/X; p) = dim X (the maximal possible value).

items.name: Classifying map of a G-cover in mod p cohomology
items.statement: Let X be a proper connected smooth C-scheme with a normal crossings divisor D, U = X − D, η̄ a geometric generic point and G a finite quotient of π_1^ét(U, η̄) (equivalently a connected G-cover Y → U). The classifying map H^i(G, F_p) → H^i(π_1^ét(U, η̄), F_p) → H^i_ét(U, F_p) is inflation followed by the edge map regarding π_1^ét-representations as étale sheaves on U.
items.note: Inflation in all degrees is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees; the étale fundamental group comes through SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (upstream PR196 ConstructibleEtale Layer 3). The edge map to étale cohomology and its multiplicativity are new.

items.name: Étale K(π,1)
items.statement: A connected C-variety U is an étale K(π,1) if the edge map H^i(π_1^ét(U, x̄), F) → H^i_ét(U, F) is an isomorphism for every i and every finite π_1-module F of p-power order (here F = F_p is what is used).

items.name: Mod p homology cover
items.statement: For U as above, the mod p homology cover Y → U is the G-cover attached to the maximal elementary abelian p-group quotient G of π_1^ét(U, η̄); then H^1(G, F_p) ≅ H^1_ét(U, F_p). When U is proper it is the pullback along the Albanese map of the multiplication-by-p cover of Alb(U).

items.name: Albanese variety and Albanese map
items.statement: For X smooth proper connected over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 with a base point x_0, Alb(X) is the abelian variety dual to Pic^0_X (reduced), with the Albanese map α_X : X → Alb(X), α_X(x_0) = 0, universal among pointed maps to abelian varieties; a point of X(C) gives a Poincaré line bundle on X × Pic^0_X.
items.locator: §1, p. 2; Proposition 2.3.10 and its proof, p. 19
items.note: Tau Ceti has abelian varieties over a field (tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianVariety) and the atlas plans Jacobians of curves (SF.3) and duals of abelian schemes (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2), but no layer plans the Albanese of a higher-dimensional variety.

items.name: Albanese dimension and maximal Albanese dimension
items.statement: The Albanese dimension of X is dim α_X(X); X has maximal Albanese dimension when dim α_X(X) = dim X.

items.name: Theorem 1: incompressibility of the mod p homology cover
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper complex variety of maximal Albanese dimension and Y → X its mod p homology cover. Then ed(Y/X; p) = dim X for all sufficiently large primes p. (Effective form: Corollary 2.3.12, item below.)

items.name: Theorem 2: lower bound from a surjective characteristic class map
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper complex variety, G a finite group and Y → X a G-cover. Suppose X has unramified good reduction at p and i < p − 2. If H^0(X, Ω^i_X) ≠ 0 and H^i(G, F_p) → H^i(X, F_p) is surjective, then ed(Y/X; p) ≥ i.
items.locator: Theorem 2, p. 3 (the case D = ∅ of Proposition 2.3.3)

items.name: Theorem 3: incompressibility of principal p-congruence covers
items.statement: Let X be an irreducible Hermitian symmetric domain and G the associated group, with Q-rank equal to R-rank. For every principal p-congruence cover Γ_1\X → Γ\X, ed(Γ_1\X → Γ\X; p) = dim X, provided, when X is not a tube domain: if X is of classical type, p > (3/2) dim X and p > dim X + 2; if X is of type E_6, p is sufficiently large.
items.locator: Theorem 3, p. 4; proved by Lemma 3.3.8, Theorem 3.3.17 and Corollary 3.3.19
items.note: Corrected statement: the printed hypothesis p > (3/2) dim X omits p > dim X + 2, which the proof needs and which differs from it only for three-dimensional ball quotients at p = 5; see sourceIssues E14.

items.name: Theorem 4: nonvanishing of restriction to Zariski opens
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper complex variety with unramified good reduction at p, i < p − 2, and W ⊂ X a dense Zariski open. Then dim_{F_p} Im(H^i(X, F_p) → H^i(W, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,i}_X = dim H^0(X, Ω^i_X).
items.note: The printed statement says only 'a Zariski open'; density is required (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: Logarithmic de Rham complex
items.statement: For X smooth over a perfect field k of characteristic p and D ⊂ X a normal crossings divisor, Ω^•_{X/k}(log D) is the de Rham complex of differentials with logarithmic poles along D; its hypercohomology is the log de Rham cohomology H^j(X, Ω^•_{X/k}(log D)).
items.note: CR.5 constructs the log differential module with residues; DD.6 develops log de Rham with its filtrations.

items.name: Frobenius twist and relative Frobenius
items.statement: X^{(1)} = X ×_{Spec k, F_k} Spec k and D^{(1)} likewise; the relative Frobenius F_{X/k} : X → X^{(1)} is a finite flat k-morphism carrying D to D^{(1)}.
items.note: DD.3 defines the Frobenius twist as a derived base change and preserves its structure map.

items.name: Logarithmic Cartier isomorphism
items.statement: For X smooth over perfect k with normal crossings divisor D, the inverse Cartier map is an isomorphism of O_{X^{(1)}}-modules C^{-1} : Ω^i_{X^{(1)}/k}(log D^{(1)}) ≅ H^i(F_{X/k*} Ω^•_{X/k}(log D)) for all i.
items.note: DD.3 compares derived Cartier with classical Cartier on smooth algebras; DD.6 carries the conjugate filtration to log objects; CR.5 supplies the Cartier-type condition.

items.name: Logarithmic Deligne–Illusie decomposition
items.statement: If (X, D) lifts to W_2(k) (in particular to a smooth formal W(k)-scheme with a relative normal crossings divisor), the lift determines an isomorphism in the derived category of O_{X^{(1)}}-modules ⊕_{i<p} Ω^i_{X^{(1)}/k}(log D^{(1)})[−i] ≅ τ_{<p} F_{X/k*} Ω^•_{X/k}(log D), inducing C^{-1} on cohomology sheaves.
items.note: DD.3 names Deligne–Illusie only as a later application with liftability and dimension bounds; no layer plans the decomposition itself.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.2: global log differentials split off de Rham cohomology
items.statement: Suppose (X, D) lifts to a smooth formal scheme over W(k) with a relative normal crossings divisor. Then for j < p, H^0(X^{(1)}, Ω^j_{X^{(1)}/k}(log D^{(1)})) is a direct summand of H^j(X, Ω^•_{X/k}(log D)): the conjugate edge map H^j(X, Ω^•(log D)) → H^0(X^{(1)}, Ω^j(log D^{(1)})) is surjective and the lift splits it.
items.note: The printed word 'canonically' refers to a splitting that depends on the lift (the proof says so); the surjection itself is canonical.

items.name: p-adic valuation and the base field K
items.statement: A p-adic valuation on a field K of characteristic 0 is a rank-one valuation v with v(p) > 0. K is assumed complete, with ring of integers O_K and perfect residue field k; K is either discretely valued or algebraically closed.
items.note: Mathlib's Valuation.RankOne (Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/RankOne.lean) is a rank-one valuation; the condition v(p) > 0 is an explicit hypothesis on top of it.

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin prism
items.statement: For K discretely valued with uniformizer π, A = W(k)[[u]] with Frobenius φ extending the Witt vector Frobenius by φ(u) = u^p, and A → O_K, u ↦ π, whose kernel is generated by the Eisenstein polynomial E(u) of π; (A, E(u)A) is the Breuil–Kisin prism. In the applications O_K = W(k), π = p, E(u) = u − p, and A/pA = k[[u]].
items.note: PR.0 lists (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) as an acceptance example. Library pieces: mathlib:WittVector, mathlib:PowerSeries, mathlib:Polynomial.IsEisensteinAt.

items.name: A_inf and Fontaine's θ
items.statement: For K algebraically closed, R = lim_{x↦x^p} O_K/p (the tilt), A_inf = W(R) with its Frobenius, and θ : A_inf → O_K the surjective ring map with θ([x]) = x̂_0 for x = (x_0, x_1, …) ∈ R and x̂_i the unique compatible lifts with x̂_i^p = x̂_{i−1}.
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean defines fontaineTheta : 𝕎 R♭ →+* R for p-adically complete R, proves θ([x]) = x.untilt and surjectivity when Frobenius is surjective on R/p (true for O_C, C algebraically closed).

items.name: The kernel of θ and the perfect prism (A_inf, ξ)
items.statement: For K algebraically closed, ker θ is principal, generated by ξ = p − [p̲] with p̲ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) ∈ R for a choice of p-power roots, and (A_inf, ξA_inf) is a perfect prism; (A_inf/p)[1/ξ] = Frac(R).
items.note: PR.0 lists (A_inf, ker θ) as an acceptance example and proves the perfect-prism/perfectoid equivalence on the existing tilt and A_inf construction.

items.name: The tilt of an algebraically closed field is algebraically closed
items.statement: If C is an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field of residue characteristic p, then Frac(O_C^♭) = C^♭ is algebraically closed.
items.note: Follows from the tilting equivalence of finite étale algebras planned in PerfectoidSpaces P1/P3.

items.name: Logarithmic formal schemes, log adic spaces and Kummer étale cohomology
items.statement: For X a formally smooth p-adic formal O_K-scheme with a relative normal crossings divisor D, X_D denotes X with the log structure of D and X_{D,K} the associated log adic space; for K algebraically closed, RΓ_két(X_{D,K}, F_p) is the cohomology of its Kummer étale site.
items.note: CR.5: fs log structures and Kummer morphisms; T6:log-sites: the Kummer étale site of log adic spaces with an ncd boundary; PR.8: the log-diamond generic fibre.

items.name: Logarithmic prismatic cohomology
items.statement: For (A, I) the Breuil–Kisin or A_inf prism with trivial log structure and X_D as above, the log prismatic cohomology RΓ_Δ(X_D/A) is a commutative algebra object of D(A) with a φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ; for D = ∅ it is the prismatic cohomology of Bhatt–Scholze.

items.name: Mod p prismatic cohomology
items.statement: RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) = RΓ_Δ(X_D/A) ⊗^L_A A/pA, with cohomology groups H^i_{Δ̄}(X_D/A), modules over A/p (= k[[u]] in the Breuil–Kisin case, = R in the A_inf case).

items.name: Mod p de Rham comparison (2.1.5(1))
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism of commutative algebras in D(k): RΓ(X_k, Ω^•_{X_k/k}(log D_k)) ≅ RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) ⊗^L_{A/pA, φ} k.

items.name: Mod p étale comparison (2.1.5(2))
items.statement: If K is algebraically closed there is an isomorphism of commutative algebras in D(F_p): RΓ_két(X_{D,K}, F_p) ≅ RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A)[1/ξ]^{φ=1}, the fibre of φ − 1 on RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A)[1/ξ].

items.name: Image of Frobenius (2.1.5(3))
items.statement: Let d generate ker(A → O_K). The linearized Frobenius φ^*RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) → RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) becomes an isomorphism in D(A/p) after inverting d, and for each i there is a canonical map V_i : H^i_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) → H^i(φ^*RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A)) with V_i ∘ φ = φ ∘ V_i = d^i.
items.note: PR.3 plans the Lη_I Frobenius factorization of BS22 §15, which gives V_i; PR.8 plans the log version under the Cartier-type hypothesis.

items.name: Completed base change (2.1.5(4))
items.statement: For a map of valued fields K → K' (each discretely valued or algebraically closed) and a Frobenius-compatible map of the corresponding prisms A → A' over O_K → O_{K'}, there is a canonical isomorphism in D(A'/p): RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) ⊗̂^L_A A' ≅ RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_{D,O_{K'}}/A'), the completion being u-adic or ξ-adic on A'.

items.name: Perfectness for proper X (2.1.5(5))
items.statement: If X is proper over O_K, RΓ_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) is a perfect complex of A/p-modules (a consequence of the Hodge–Tate comparison).

items.name: Frobenius modules over an algebraically closed field
items.statement: Let L be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and M a finite-dimensional L-vector space with a φ-semilinear map whose linearization is bijective. Then 1 − φ is surjective on M and M^{φ=1} ⊗_{F_p} L → M is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.1.6, p. 9, citing [Katz73, Prop. 4.1.1]
items.note: Lang-type statement; no library declaration or layer found.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.6: étale comparison for proper X, degreewise
items.statement: Suppose K is algebraically closed and X is proper over O_K. Then for each i ≥ 0 there is a natural isomorphism H^i_két(X_{D,K}, F_p) ⊗_{F_p} (A/pA)[1/ξ] ≅ H^i_{Δ̄}(X_D/A)[1/ξ].

items.name: Derived complete complexes and modules
items.statement: With d as in 2.1.5(3), C ∈ D(A/p) is derived complete if C → Rlim_n (C ⊗^L_{A/p} A/(p, d^n)A) is a quasi-isomorphism; a module is derived complete if it is so as a one-term complex; C is derived complete iff all H^i(C) are.

items.name: Completed derived base change
items.statement: For an A/p-module M and A → A' as in 2.1.5(4), M ⊗̂^L_A A' = Rlim_n M ⊗^L_{A/p} A'/(p, d^n)A'.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.8(1)–(2): completed base change of derived complete modules
items.statement: With the notation of 2.1.5(4) and K discretely valued: (1) if M is a derived complete A/p-module then M ⊗̂^L_A A' is concentrated in degree 0; (2) the functor M ↦ H^0(M ⊗̂^L_A A') on derived complete A/p-modules is exact.
items.note: The proof uses a continuous splitting of finitely generated saturated A/p-submodules N ⊂ A'/p; the printed choice of the splitting projects onto the wrong summand (sourceIssues E1). 2.1.9 records that the discretely valued hypothesis is not known to be removable.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.8(3): degreewise base change of mod p prismatic cohomology
items.statement: With K discretely valued: H^i_{Δ̄}(X_{D,O_{K'}}/A') ≅ H^0(H^i_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) ⊗̂^L_A A').

items.name: Lemma 2.2.1: small Frobenius height forces torsion-freeness
items.statement: Let M be a finitely generated k[[u]]-module with a Frobenius-semilinear φ : M → M and a linear V : M → φ^*M such that φ ∘ V = V ∘ φ = u^d. If d + 1 < p then M is torsion-free.

items.name: The invariants h^{0,i}_{X,D}
items.statement: With K = W(k)[1/p], X a proper smooth formal O_K-scheme with relative normal crossings divisor D (2.2.2), h^{0,i}_{X,D} = dim_K H^0(X_K, Ω^i_{X_K/K}(log D)); for a smooth scheme Y over a field with ncd D, h^{0,i}_{Y,D} = dim H^0(Y, Ω^i_Y(log D)).

items.name: Upper semicontinuity of h^0 in a proper flat family
items.statement: For a proper smooth X over a discrete valuation ring with special fibre X_k and generic fibre X_K, and D a relative normal crossings divisor, dim_k H^0(X_k, Ω^i(log D_k)) ≥ dim_K H^0(X_K, Ω^i(log D_K)).
items.locator: End of proof of Proposition 2.2.3, p. 12
items.note: Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 2 plans the cohomology-and-base-change theorem, Grauert's theorem and upper semicontinuity for coherent sheaves under proper flat morphisms over locally Noetherian bases; Ω^i(log D) is locally free.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.3: restriction to a dense open formal subscheme
items.statement: In the setting 2.2.2 (K = W(k)[1/p], C ⊃ K algebraically closed complete, X proper smooth formal O_K-scheme with relative ncd D), let W ⊂ X − D be a dense open formal subscheme. Then for 0 ≤ i < p − 2, dim_{F_p} Im(H^i_két(X_{D,C}, F_p) → H^i_ét(W_C, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,i}_{X,D}.

items.name: Corollary 2.2.6: the boundary case i = p − 2
items.statement: If H^{i+1}_{Δ̄}(X_D/A) is u-torsion-free, the conclusion of Proposition 2.2.3 holds for i ≤ p − 2. In particular it holds for i ≤ p − 2 when X is the formal completion of an abelian scheme over O_K and D = ∅.

items.name: Mod p prismatic cohomology of an abelian scheme
items.statement: For X the formal completion of an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over O_K and A the Breuil–Kisin prism, H^•_{Δ̄}(X/A) is the exterior algebra over k[[u]] on H^1_{Δ̄}(X/A), which is free of rank 2g.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 2.2.6, p. 12, citing [AL23, Prop. 4.58, Cor. 4.64]
items.note: Extracted as PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23/104 and routed there to the proposed Part II on prismatic Dieudonné theory; routed to the same Part II here.

items.name: The invariants h^{0,1→i}
items.statement: h^{0,1→i}_{X,D} = dim_K Im(∧^i H^0(X_K, Ω^1(log D)) → H^0(X_K, Ω^i(log D))) and h^{0,1→i}_{X_k,D_k} = dim_k Im(∧^i H^0(X_k, Ω^1(log D_k)) → H^0(X_k, Ω^i(log D_k))), the maps being wedge product.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.8: restriction of cup products of degree-one classes
items.statement: In the setting 2.2.2, let W ⊂ X − D be a dense open formal subscheme and p > max{i + 1, 3}. Then dim_{F_p} Im(∧^i H^1_két(X_{D,C}, F_p) → H^i_ét(W_C, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,1→i}_{X_k,D_k}, the map being cup product followed by restriction.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.10: log, adic and open étale cohomology agree
items.statement: Let C be algebraically closed complete p-adic, Y a proper smooth C-scheme with normal crossings divisor D and U = Y − D. Then H^i_két(Y^ad_{D^ad}, F_p) ≅ H^i_két(Y_D, F_p) ≅ H^i_ét(U, F_p) naturally, for all i ≥ 0.

items.name: Kummer étale direct images and logarithmic purity
items.statement: For ε : Y_{D,két} → Y_ét (Y smooth, D normal crossings, over a field of characteristic 0) and M = Rε_*F_p: H^i_ét(Y, M) ≅ H^i_két(Y_D, F_p) and H^i_két(Y_D, F_p) ≅ H^i_ét(Y − D, F_p) ([Ill02, Thms 7.2, 7.4, Cor 7.5]); the pullback M^ad to Y^ad_ét computes Kummer étale cohomology of the log adic space (Y^ad, D^ad) ([DLLZ19, Lemma 4.6.2]).
items.note: PR.8 and CohomologyComparisons CP.4 insist Kummer étale and ordinary étale cohomology be compared, but no layer plans this purity theorem.

items.name: Huber's comparison of algebraic and adic étale cohomology
items.statement: For a proper scheme Y over an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field and a torsion étale sheaf M, H^i_ét(Y, M) ≅ H^i_ét(Y^ad, M^ad).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.2.10, p. 14, citing [Hub96, Prop. 2.1.4, Thm 3.8.1]

items.name: Proposition 2.2.11(a): restriction for proper smooth O_K-schemes
items.statement: Let X be a proper smooth O_K-scheme with relative ncd D, U = X ∖ D and W ⊂ U_C a dense open subscheme. If 0 ≤ i < p − 2 then dim_{F_p} Im(H^i_ét(U_C, F_p) → H^i_ét(W, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,i}_{X_C,D_C}.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.11(b): the abelian scheme case
items.statement: If X is an abelian scheme over O_K and D = ∅, the inequality of 2.2.11(a) holds for i ≤ p − 2.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.11(c): the cup-product version
items.statement: With X, D, U, W as in 2.2.11(a), if p > max{i + 1, 3} then dim_{F_p} Im(∧^i H^1_ét(U_C, F_p) → H^i_ét(W, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,1→i}_{X_k,D_k}.

items.name: Good reduction and unramified good reduction of (Y, D)
items.statement: For C algebraically closed of characteristic 0, Y proper smooth over C and D ⊂ Y a normal crossings divisor, (Y, D) has good reduction at p if for some p-adic valuation on C (not necessarily complete) with ring O_C, Y extends to a smooth proper O_C-scheme Y° with a relative ncd D° extending D; it has unramified good reduction if (Y°, D°) can be chosen to descend to an absolutely unramified discrete valuation ring O ⊂ O_C. Then h^{0,1→i}_{Y,D,p} is the maximum of h^{0,1→i}_{Y°_k,D°_k} over all such (Y°, D°), k the residue field of O.

items.name: Invariance of étale cohomology under extension of algebraically closed fields
items.statement: For C ⊂ C' algebraically closed and a C-variety U, H^i_ét(U, F_p) → H^i_ét(U_{C'}, F_p) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Upstream PR196 EtaleBaseChange Layer 4 (smooth base change: invariance under extension of separably closed base fields), integrated through SF.2.

items.name: Corollary 2.2.13(a): restriction over an arbitrary algebraically closed field
items.statement: Let Y be proper smooth over C (algebraically closed, characteristic 0), D ⊂ Y a normal crossings divisor, W ⊂ U = Y − D a dense open, and suppose (Y, D) has unramified good reduction at p. If 0 ≤ i < p − 2 then dim_{F_p} Im(H^i_ét(U, F_p) → H^i_ét(W, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,i}_{Y,D}.

items.name: Corollary 2.2.13(b): abelian varieties at i = p − 2
items.statement: If Y is an abelian variety over C (and D = ∅) with unramified good reduction at p, the inequality of 2.2.13(a) holds for i ≤ p − 2.
items.note: Printed as 'abelian scheme' (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Corollary 2.2.13(c): the cup-product version
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of 2.2.13(a), if p > max{i + 1, 3} then dim_{F_p} Im(∧^i H^1_ét(U, F_p) → H^i_ét(W, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,1→i}_{Y,D,p}.

items.name: Generic members of good moduli have unramified good reduction everywhere
items.statement: Let M be a smooth, faithfully flat, connected, separated Deligne–Mumford stack over Z, 𝒴 → M proper smooth with a relative ncd 𝒟 ⊂ 𝒴. If Spec C → M has image the generic point of M, then (𝒴 ×_M Spec C, 𝒟 ×_M Spec C) has unramified good reduction at every prime p. (No open substack has this property unless 𝒟 = ∅.)
items.note: Uses étale presentations of Deligne–Mumford stacks, planned in SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1.

items.name: Spreading out and reducedness modulo p
items.statement: If (Y, D) is proper smooth with ncd over C, it descends to a proper smooth scheme with relative ncd over a finite-type normal Z-subalgebra 𝒜 ⊂ C; since 𝒜 ⊗ Q is geometrically reduced, 𝒜/p𝒜 is reduced for p ≫ 0, and for p ≫ 0 there is a height-one prime 𝔭 over p with 𝒜_𝔭 a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer p.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 2.2.15, p. 16, citing [EGA IV, 4.6.1, 9.7.7]
items.note: Limit and constructibility arguments of EGA IV §§8–9 belong to the scheme foundations (SF.0–SF.4); SF.4 owns models over bases.

items.name: Étale cohomology of the generic point as a colimit
items.statement: For an integral C-variety U with generic point η, H^i(η, F_p) = colim_{W} H^i_ét(W, F_p) over dense opens W ⊂ U, and H^i(η, F_p) is the Galois cohomology of the function field.
items.locator: Corollary 2.2.15 and proof of Proposition 2.3.3, pp. 15–17

items.name: Corollary 2.2.15(a): restriction to the generic point
items.statement: Let Y be proper smooth over C, D a normal crossings divisor, U = Y − D and η the generic point. For i ≥ 0 and p ≫ 0, dim_{F_p} Im(H^i_ét(U, F_p) → H^i_ét(η, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,i}_{Y,D}.

items.name: Corollary 2.2.15(b): cup products at the generic point
items.statement: In the setting of 2.2.15(a), for p ≫ 0, dim_{F_p} Im(∧^i H^1_ét(U, F_p) → H^i_ét(η, F_p)) ≥ h^{0,1→i}_{Y,D,p}.

items.name: Transfer for finite extensions of degree prime to p
items.statement: If η'/η is a finite separable extension of fields of degree prime to p, restriction H^i(η, F_p) → H^i(η', F_p) is injective, because corestriction ∘ restriction is multiplication by the degree.
items.note: Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology plans corestriction in all degrees with cor ∘ res = index.

items.name: Affine Artin vanishing
items.statement: If Z is an affine variety over an algebraically closed field and dim Z < i, then H^i_ét(Z, F) = 0 for every torsion sheaf F (with torsion invertible on the base).
items.note: Upstream PR196 EtaleBaseChange Layer 6 (affine Artin vanishing bound q > dim X), integrated through SF.2.

items.name: Equivariant form of essential dimension [FKW21, 2.1.4]
items.statement: If ed(Y'/U') < i for a G-cover Y' → U', then there are a dense open W ⊂ U', a map of C-schemes W → Z with dim Z < i and a G-cover Y'_Z → Z with Y'|_W ≅ Y'_Z ×_Z W as W-schemes with G-action; shrinking, Z may be taken affine.
items.note: From the authors' earlier paper (Compositio 2021), listed under prerequisites.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.3: the characteristic class lower bound
items.statement: Let X be a proper connected smooth C-scheme with normal crossings divisor D, U = X − D, and suppose i < p − 2 and (X, D) has unramified good reduction at p. Let G be a finite group and Y → U a G-cover. If h^{0,i}_{X,D} ≠ 0 and H^i(G, F_p) → H^i_ét(U, F_p) is surjective, then ed(Y/U; p) ≥ i. If X is an abelian variety and D = ∅, the same holds for i ≤ p − 2.

items.name: Mod p cohomology of abelian varieties and tori
items.statement: For an abelian variety A of dimension g over an algebraically closed field C of characteristic 0, H^•_ét(A, F_p) is the exterior algebra on H^1_ét(A, F_p) ≅ Hom(π_1^ét(A), F_p) ≅ F_p^{2g}, and the same holds for a split torus G_m^t with H^1 of rank t; multiplication by p on A is a Galois cover with group A[p] ≅ (Z/p)^{2g} and both are étale K(π,1)'s.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 2.3.5, p. 18; proof of Lemma 3.2.2, p. 24
items.note: Via Artin comparison (SF.2, PR196 ComplexComparison Layer 10) and Künneth for tori (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology#stage-5-bundles-covers-products-and-finite-cover-descent); [n] is planned in AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A3.

items.name: Corollary 2.3.5: Brosnan's conjecture for p ≥ g + 2
items.statement: Let X/C be an abelian variety of dimension g, p ≥ g + 2 a prime at which X has unramified good reduction, and X' → X the multiplication-by-p map viewed as a (Z/p)^{2g}-cover. Then ed(X'/X; p) = g. In particular this holds for all p ≫ 0.

items.name: Theorem 2.3.8: lower bound for the mod p homology cover
items.statement: Suppose (X, D) has unramified good reduction at p and p > max{dim X + 1, 3}. Then the mod p homology cover Y → U satisfies ed(Y/U; p) ≥ max{i : h^{0,1→i}_{X,D,p} > 0}. In particular, for p ≫ 0, ed(Y/U; p) ≥ max{i : h^{0,1→i}_{X,D} > 0}.

items.name: Albanese dimension as a Hodge-theoretic invariant
items.statement: For X smooth proper over C (D = ∅), max{i : h^{0,1→i}_X > 0} = dim α_X(X): H^0(X, Ω^1_X) ≅ H^0(Alb(X), Ω^1), these forms generate the global i-forms on Alb(X), and X is generically smooth over α_X(X) since char C = 0.
items.note: Printed with H^1(X, Ω^1) for H^0(X, Ω^1) (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Koizumi: good reduction of the Albanese and Picard varieties
items.statement: If X has a smooth proper model X° over a discrete valuation ring O, then Alb(X) and Pic^0_X extend to abelian schemes over O.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.3.10, p. 19, citing [Koi60, Thm 2]

items.name: Proposition 2.3.10(1): the Albanese map extends over a good model
items.statement: Let p be a prime of good unramified reduction for X, with smooth proper model X° over O_C as in 2.2.12. Then α_X extends to α°_X : X° → Alb(X)° over O_C with Alb(X)° an abelian scheme: the Poincaré bundle on X × A (A = Pic^0_X) extends to X° × A° by regularity, giving X° → Pic^0_{A°} ≅ A°∨ ≅ Alb(X)°.

items.name: Proposition 2.3.10(2): effective bound for the mod p homology cover
items.statement: In the setting of 2.3.10(1), let i = dim α_X(X) and suppose p > max{i + 1, 3}. If the special fibre of X° is generically smooth over its image under α°_X, then the mod p homology cover Y → X satisfies ed(Y/X; p) ≥ dim α_X(X).
items.note: Corrected statement: the printed proposition omits p > max{i + 1, 3}, which its appeal to Theorem 2.3.8 requires (sourceIssues E15).

items.name: Albanese map unramified at p
items.statement: α_X is unramified at p if O_C and X° in 2.2.12 can be chosen so that the special fibre of X° is generically étale over its image under α°_X.

items.name: Corollary 2.3.12: effective incompressibility for maximal Albanese dimension
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper C-scheme of maximal Albanese dimension and Y → X its mod p homology cover. If p > max{dim X + 1, 3} is a prime of unramified good reduction for X at which α_X is unramified, then ed(Y/X; p) = dim X. In particular this holds for p ≫ 0.
items.note: Corrected statement: the bound p > max{dim X + 1, 3} is missing in print (sourceIssues E15).

items.name: Cohomology ring of an elementary abelian p-group
items.statement: For p odd and H̄ an elementary abelian p-group, H^•(H̄, F_p) ≅ ∧^•H̄^*(1) ⊗ Sym^•H̄^*(2), where H̄^*(1) = H^1(H̄, F_p) sits in degree 1 and H̄^*(2) = β(H^1(H̄, F_p)) is its Bockstein image in degree 2.
items.locator: 3.1.1, p. 20; proof of Proposition 3.1.9, p. 23 ([BC92, §10]; [AM04, II Cor. 4.3])
items.note: Mathlib has group cohomology (mathlib:groupCohomology) and H^1 with trivial action (mathlib:groupCohomology.H1IsoOfIsTrivial), but no cohomology ring computation.

items.name: Central extensions of elementary abelian p-groups
items.statement: For elementary abelian p-groups H, N (p odd) with trivial action, H^2(H, N) ≅ H^2(H, F_p) ⊗ N ≅ (∧^2 H^* ⊗ N) ⊕ (H^* ⊗ N), the first summand the image of cup products of degree-one classes, the second the image of the Bockstein; this group classifies central extensions 0 → N → E → H → 0.

items.name: The central extension attached to a 2-cocycle
items.statement: For c ∈ Z^2(H, N) (trivial action) the group E_c has underlying set N × H and law (n_1, h_1)(n_2, h_2) = (n_1 + n_2 + c(h_1, h_2), h_1 + h_2); cohomologous cocycles give isomorphic extensions and Baer sum corresponds to addition.
items.note: Mathlib has the extension structure (mathlib:GroupExtension) and 2-cocycles, but not this construction and classification.

items.name: Finite Heisenberg group
items.statement: A central extension 0 → N → E → H → 0 of elementary abelian p-groups is a finite Heisenberg group if its class in H^2(H, N) is represented by an alternating bilinear form H ⊗ H → N.

items.name: Weights of F_p^× and Z_p^× actions
items.statement: An F_p-vector space V with F_p^×-action has weight n ∈ Z/(p − 1) if α acts by α^{−n}; V_n is the weight-n summand. A finite free Z_p-module with Z_p^×-action has weight n ∈ Z if α acts by α^{−n}.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.2: characterizations of finite Heisenberg groups
items.statement: For p odd and a central extension 0 → N → E → H → 0 of elementary abelian p-groups, the following are equivalent: (i) E is a finite Heisenberg group; (ii) its class lies in ∧^2 H^* ⊗ N; (iii) E has exponent p; (iv) the extension admits an F_p^×-action with H of weight −1 and N of weight −2. In particular being Heisenberg depends only on the group E.
items.note: Exponent: mathlib:Monoid.exponent. The proof of (ii)⇒(i) prints n_i ∈ N_i for n_i ∈ N (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Lemma 3.1.5(i): pro-p central extensions of free abelian groups are alternating
items.statement: For a central extension 0 → N → E → H → 0 with N ≅ Z_p^r, H ≅ Z_p^s (finitely generated free abelian pro-p groups), H^2(H, N) ≅ Λ^2_{Z_p} H^* ⊗ N, so the class of E is represented by an alternating bilinear form.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.5(ii): the Z_p^× weight action
items.statement: Every E as in Lemma 3.1.5(i) admits a Z_p^×-action by group automorphisms under which H has weight −1 and N has weight −2.

items.name: Cohomology of free abelian pro-p groups
items.statement: For a finitely generated free abelian pro-p group F and a finite elementary abelian p-group M with trivial F-action, H^•(F, M) ≅ (∧^• H^1(F, F_p)) ⊗ M.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for profinite groups
items.statement: For a closed normal subgroup N of a profinite group E with quotient H and a discrete E-module M there is a spectral sequence E_2^{i,j} = H^i(H, H^j(N, M)) ⇒ H^{i+j}(E, M), functorial in automorphisms of the extension; for M = F_p it is multiplicative (E_r is a differential graded algebra).
items.locator: Lemma 3.1.6 and proof of Proposition 3.1.9, pp. 22–23; proof of Lemma 3.2.2, p. 24
items.note: R02.2 plans the spectral sequence for closed normal subgroups; its multiplicative structure and equivariance under automorphisms of the extension are the API the Heisenberg Part II needs from it.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.6: E_3-degeneration by weights
items.statement: For E as in Lemma 3.1.5 the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence E_2^{i,j} = H^i(H, H^j(N, F_p)) ⇒ H^{i+j}(E, F_p) degenerates at E_3 if p ≥ min{rk N + 1, rk H}.

items.name: Reduction mod p of a pro-p central extension
items.statement: A reduction mod p of E as in (3.1.4) is a map of central extensions to 0 → N̄ → Ē → H̄ → 0 identifying N̄ = N/pN and H̄ = H/pH, with Ē a finite Heisenberg group.

items.name: Lemma 3.1.8: existence and uniqueness of the mod p reduction
items.statement: Every central extension E as in (3.1.4) admits a mod p reduction Ē, and the extension class of Ē is uniquely determined by that of E.

items.name: Proposition 3.1.9: surjectivity of inflation from the Heisenberg quotient
items.statement: Let E be as in (3.1.4) and Ē a mod p reduction. If p > (rk_{Z_p} H + 3 rk_{Z_p} N + 1)/2, then the ring map H^•(Ē, F_p) → H^•(E, F_p) is surjective.
items.note: The proof prints (E_3^{i,j})_{i+2j} for (Ē_3^{i,j})_{i+2j} (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Maximal pro-p quotient
items.statement: For a profinite group G, G^p denotes its maximal pro-p quotient.

items.name: Torus torsors over an abelian variety
items.statement: For a split torus T ≅ G_m^t and an abelian variety S over C, a T-torsor U → S; by Hilbert 90 it is Zariski-locally trivial and, after choosing a basis of X^*(T), corresponds to line bundles L_1, …, L_t on S.
items.note: Line bundles and Picard objects are imported from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3; torsors under tori over abelian varieties are not planned.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.2(a): fundamental group of a torus torsor
items.statement: For U → S a T-torsor over an abelian variety and x̄ ↦ s̄, π_1^ét(U, x̄) is a central extension 0 → π_1^ét(U_s̄, x̄) → π_1^ét(U, x̄) → π_1^ét(S, s̄) → 0 of free abelian profinite groups, whose maximal pro-p quotient is again exact, and H^•(π_1^ét(U)^p, F_p) → H^•(π_1^ét(U), F_p) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.2(b): torus torsors over abelian varieties are étale K(π,1)'s
items.statement: The C-scheme U of Lemma 3.2.2(a) is an étale K(π,1).

items.name: The Heisenberg cover U(Ē) of a torus torsor
items.statement: A mod p reduction Ē of the pro-p extension π_1^ét(U)^p gives a surjection π_1^ét(U, x̄) ↠ Ē onto a finite Heisenberg group and the corresponding finite cover U(Ē) → U.

items.name: Good reduction of a torus torsor over an abelian variety
items.statement: U → S has good reduction at p if for some p-adic valuation on C with ring O_C, U → S extends to a T-torsor U° → S° over an abelian scheme over O_C; unramified good reduction if U° → S° can be chosen to descend to an absolutely unramified discrete valuation ring O ⊂ O_C.

items.name: Logarithmic top forms on torus embeddings over abelian varieties
items.statement: For a torus embedding (X, D) over an abelian variety S of dimension r with dense T-torsor U, ω_T = dz_1/z_1 ∧ … ∧ dz_t/z_t is T-invariant and independent of trivializations up to sign, and ω_r ⊗ ω_T ∈ H^0(X, Ω^d_X(log D)) is nonzero for a nonzero r-form ω_r on S; hence h^{0,d}_{X,D} ≠ 0, d = dim X. For the compactification P = P(O ⊕ L_1^∨) ×_S … ×_S P(O ⊕ L_t^∨) of U, P is smooth projective over S and D = P − U is a normal crossings divisor.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.2.7, p. 25; proof of Proposition 3.2.14, p. 28
items.note: The proof of 3.2.14 prints ω_r ⊗ ω_s (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.7: incompressibility of Heisenberg covers of torus torsors
items.statement: Let U → S be a T-torsor over an abelian variety with unramified good reduction at p, and suppose p > dim U + (dim U_s̄ + 1)/2 and p > dim U + 2. Then ed(U(Ē)/U; p) = dim U.
items.note: Corrected statement: the printed hypothesis omits p > dim U + 2, which the appeal to Proposition 2.3.3 (i = dim U < p − 2) requires; it is implied by the printed bound only when dim U_s̄ ≥ 3 (sourceIssues E14).

items.name: Toric varieties and relative torus embeddings
items.statement: A toric variety (torus embedding) over a field k is a normal k-scheme with an action of a split torus T having a dense open orbit that is a T-torsor; these are described by fans Σ of rational polyhedral cones in X_*(T)_Q, and proper ones by complete fans. A fan defines X(Σ) over Z. For a scheme S, X → S with T-action is a torus embedding over S if Zariski-locally on S it is T-equivariantly X(Σ) ×_Z S; it contains an open T-torsor U dense in every fibre, and D = X − U is its boundary.
items.note: Fans themselves are in the library: tauceti:TauCeti.Toric.Fan (finite fans of toric cones), tauceti:TauCeti.Toric.Fan.IsComplete, tauceti:TauCeti.Toric.Fan.IsRegular. AnalyticToricGeometry Layer 0 glues the toric scheme over C; ShimuraCompactifications C0 extends the charts to the base rings of integral models and builds torus embeddings relative to a torus torsor.

items.name: Étale-local torus embeddings are Zariski-local
items.statement: Aut_T(X(Σ) ×_Z S) = Aut_T(U(Σ) × S) = T(S); hence an X → S étale-locally isomorphic to X(Σ) × S is a twist by a T-torsor, which is Zariski-locally trivial, so X → S is a torus embedding.
items.note: C0 constructs torus embeddings relative to a torus torsor by descent.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.9: classification of relative torus embeddings
items.statement: For S irreducible and T fixed, torus embeddings X → S with a dense open T-torsor are equivalent to pairs (U, Σ) of a T-torsor U over S and a fan Σ in X_*(T)_Q, via X ↦ (U, fan of X_η) and (U, Σ) ↦ (X(Σ) × U)/T.

items.name: Boundary strata and iterated blow-ups of torus embeddings
items.statement: For a torus embedding X → S over a C-scheme S, the boundary D has the stratification D_0 ⊂ D_1 ⊂ … with D_j locally S × (closure of the j-dimensional T-orbits of X_0); D_0 is étale over S, finite étale if X is proper. X^1 → X is the blow-up of D_0, again a torus embedding with boundary D^1, smooth with relative ncd if X is; iterating gives X ← X^1 ← X^2 ← …, and X̂^i denotes the completion of X^i along D^i.
items.note: Orbit strata are planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AnalyticToricGeometry#layer-4-torus-actions-strata-and-the-boundary and star subdivisions in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AnalyticToricGeometry#layer-5-toric-maps-and-properness; the relative iterated blow-up of the zero-dimensional strata and its formal completions are new.

items.name: Smoothness criterion and toric resolution
items.statement: A torus embedding X(Σ) × S over a smooth S is smooth with relative normal crossings boundary iff every cone of Σ is regular [KKMS73, II.2, Thm 4*]; every fan has a regular subdivision, and subdivisions (in particular blow-ups of torus-invariant strata) give proper torus-equivariant modifications [Ful93, p. 48].
items.locator: Lemma 3.2.11 proof, p. 27; proof of Proposition 3.2.14, p. 28
items.note: Regular cones and subdivisions are in the library (tauceti:TauCeti.Toric.IsRegularCone, tauceti:TauCeti.Toric.Fan.IsSubdivision); C0 plans sufficiently fine smooth refinements and ATG Layer 5 properness of subdivisions.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.11: good reduction passes from the torsor to the torus embedding
items.statement: Let X/S be a smooth torus embedding with normal crossings boundary D. If the T-torsor U has unramified good reduction at p, then (X, D) has unramified good reduction at p.

items.name: Lemma 3.2.12: separating a zero-dimensional stratum from a divisor
items.statement: Let S and X/S be smooth with D ⊂ X a relative normal crossings divisor, Z ⊂ X̂ a formal subscheme of codimension 1 and Z^i ⊂ X̂^i its proper transforms. Then there are a dense open W ⊂ S and i ≥ 1 with D_0^i|_W ⊄ Z^i.
items.note: The proof prints a_I for a_J (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Complex analytic spaces and their Zariski topology
items.statement: For a complex analytic space Y, a Zariski closed subset is a closed subset locally cut out by analytic functions, and a Zariski open subset is the complement of one; Zariski openness is not transitive along open embeddings of analytic spaces.
items.note: Complex analytic spaces and analytification are upstream PR196 ComplexComparison Layer 2 (integrated through SF.2), which ComplexComparisonPartII C0 builds on.

items.name: Compact homotopy cores of complex varieties
items.statement: A (smooth) complex algebraic variety W contains a compact subset W^- whose inclusion is a homotopy equivalence.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.2.14, p. 28, citing [Łoj64, Thm 4]
items.note: To be derived from the finite triangulation compatible with a stratification planned in upstream PR196 ComplexComparison Layers 3–4 (through SF.2).

items.name: Proposition 3.2.14: nonvanishing on tubular neighbourhoods of the boundary
items.statement: Let S be an abelian variety over C, X/S a proper torus embedding with boundary D and dense open T-torsor U, d = dim X, and suppose U/S has unramified good reduction at a prime p > d + 2. Let V ⊂ X^an be an analytic open subset containing D^an and V' ⊂ V a dense Zariski open subset of V. Then H^d(U, F_p) → H^d(U ∩ V', F_p) is nonzero.
items.note: Corrected statement: the printed proposition asks only that V' be non-empty, which is false for disconnected V (sourceIssues E13). Theorem 3.3.17 needs the variant for a non-complete fan (sourceIssues E16).

items.name: Analytic essential dimension and p-essential dimension
items.statement: For a finite map V_1 → V of reduced complex analytic spaces, ed(V_1/V) is the least e such that for some dense Zariski open V' ⊂ V there are a finite map Y_1 → Y of analytic spaces with dim Y = e and a map V' → Y with V_1|_{V'} ≅ the normalization of V' ×_Y Y_1; ed(V_1/V; p) is the minimum of ed(Ṽ_1/Ṽ) over finite Ṽ → V of degree prime to p (degree taken over a Zariski open where it is finite flat), with Ṽ_1 the normalization of Ṽ ×_V V_1. Auxiliary covers need not be étale.
items.note: For the proof of 3.2.17 the compressions must go through Stein spaces Y carrying Ē-coverings (sourceIssues E17).

items.name: Normalization of complex analytic spaces and of finite covers
items.statement: Reduced complex analytic spaces have normalizations; for a finite map Y_1 → Y and V' → Y the normalization of V' ×_Y Y_1 exists, and X(Ē) → X denotes the normalization of X in U(Ē) → U.

items.name: Transfer for finite analytic covers of degree prime to p
items.statement: If Ṽ' → V' is a finite surjective map of normal complex analytic spaces of degree prime to p, then H^d(V', F_p) → H^d(Ṽ', F_p) is injective (a trace map composes with pullback to multiplication by the degree).

items.name: Vanishing above the dimension for Stein spaces
items.statement: If Y is a Stein space of complex dimension n, then H^k(Y, F_p) = 0 for k > n.
items.note: Andreotti–Frankel treat Stein manifolds; singular Stein spaces are Narasimhan's theorem (sourceIssues E18).

items.name: Corollary 3.2.17: analytic incompressibility near the boundary
items.statement: With the assumptions of Proposition 3.2.14, suppose p > dim U + (dim U_s̄ + 1)/2, and let V(Ē) = X(Ē)^an|_V. Then ed(V(Ē)/V; p) = d, where compressions are taken through Stein bases Y carrying Ē-coverings Y_1 → Y (this contains every compression obtained from an affine algebraic one).
items.note: Corrected scope: the printed proof shrinks Y to a Stein space and treats Y_1 → Y as an Ē-covering, neither of which Definition 3.2.15 provides (sourceIssues E17).

items.name: Corollary 3.2.18: the case of a torus (Burda)
items.statement: If in Corollary 3.2.17 dim S = 0, its conclusion holds with no restriction on p: then π_1^ét(U) is abelian, Ē = π_1^ét(U)/p and H^•(U, F_p) is generated in degree 1.

items.name: Shimura datum and Shimura variety
items.statement: A Shimura datum (G, X): a reductive Q-group G and a G(R)-conjugacy class X of homomorphisms h : S = Res_{C/R} G_m → G_R satisfying Deligne's axioms; X is a Hermitian symmetric domain and for neat compact open K ⊂ G(A_f), Sh_K(G, X) = G(Q)\X × G(A_f)/K is a complex algebraic variety.

items.name: The Hodge cocharacter μ_h
items.statement: For h ∈ X, μ_h : G_m → G_C is the composite of G_m → S_C (from R ⊗_R C = R ⊕ c^*(R)) with h; it is minuscule and, by the axioms, nontrivial.

items.name: Dynkin diagram with Galois action and the opposition involution
items.statement: For G with G^ad Q-simple, the Dynkin diagram Δ(G) carries a transitive action of Gal(Q̄/Q); the opposition involution of the root system is −w_0 for the longest Weyl element w_0.
items.note: The absolute root datum with Galois action is planned in Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7; the longest element is in the library (tauceti:TauCeti.longestElement).

items.name: The field K_Δ of a Shimura datum
items.statement: For (G, X) a Shimura datum with G^ad Q-simple, the kernel of the Galois action on Δ(G) cuts out a field K_Δ that is CM or totally real, complex conjugation acts on Δ(G) by the opposition involution, and K_Δ is totally real exactly when −1 ∈ W_G.

items.name: Fundamental coweights and parabolics attached to cocharacters
items.statement: For a maximal torus T ⊂ G^ad and positive roots, μ_α ∈ X_*(T) is the coweight equal to 1 on the simple root α and 0 on the others, μ_R = ∏_{α∈R} μ_α for R ⊂ Δ(G), with conjugacy class [μ_R] independent of choices; P_R is the parabolic whose Lie algebra is the sum of the root spaces on which μ_R is non-negative ([SGA3, XXVI 1.4]).
items.note: Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7 keeps the dynamic approach to parabolics, Levi subgroups and unipotent radicals.

items.name: The special nodes Σ and Σ̃
items.statement: Since μ_h is minuscule it corresponds to a set of vertices Σ ⊂ Δ(G) with at most one element in each connected component; Σ̃ = Σ ∪ c(Σ) for complex conjugation c.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.3: structure of the unipotent radical U_Σ̃
items.statement: For μ_Σ̃ ∈ [μ_Σ̃] with parabolic P_Σ̃ and unipotent radical U_Σ̃: U_Σ̃ is a central extension of vector groups 0 → Z(U_Σ̃) → U_Σ̃ → U_Σ̃/Z(U_Σ̃) → 0, U_Σ̃ = Z(U_Σ̃) if c fixes Σ, and w = μ_Σ μ_{c(Σ)} acts with weight 2 on Z(U_Σ̃) and weight 1 on U_Σ̃/Z(U_Σ̃).
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications C1 plans unipotent radicals, their centres and the weight filtration of boundary mixed data; what is new is the Dynkin-diagram description through Σ̃ and its identification with the parabolic of a zero-dimensional rational boundary component.

items.name: Condition 3.3.5: a rational cocharacter in [μ_Σ̃]
items.statement: Condition (3.3.5): the conjugacy class [μ_Σ̃] contains a cocharacter defined over Q; it implies that [μ_Σ̃] is Gal(Q̄/Q)-stable.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.6: rational cocharacters and rational parabolics
items.statement: [μ_Σ̃] contains a cocharacter defined over Q if and only if [P_Σ̃] contains a parabolic subgroup defined over Q.
items.note: Rigidity and lifting of cocharacters of tori are planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups#layer-4-jordan-decomposition-diagonalizable-groups-tori.

items.name: Q-simple adjoint Shimura groups are restrictions of scalars
items.statement: If (G, X) is a Shimura datum with G^ad Q-simple, then G^ad = Res_{F/Q} G_0 for a totally real field F and an absolutely simple F-group G_0.

items.name: Real boundary parabolics
items.statement: For the absolutely simple real factor G_{0,R}, the conjugacy class of the parabolic attached to μ_{Σ̃_0} contains a parabolic defined over R (the parabolic of a real boundary component of X_0).
items.note: V2 constructs the boundary components for Baily–Borel; C1 attaches their parabolics.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.8: criteria for condition 3.3.5
items.statement: Suppose G^ad is Q-simple, so G^ad = Res_{F/Q} G_0. If (1) Σ̃ is Gal(Q̄/Q)-stable and (2) for some (hence, by (1), every) embedding F → R the F-rank of G_0 equals its R-rank, then condition 3.3.5 holds.

items.name: Explicit forms of conditions (1) and (2)
items.statement: (1) implies X ≅ X_0^m for an irreducible Hermitian domain X_0, and is equivalent to it unless X_0 is of type D_n^H with n even. For G of type B, C or D_n with n even, −1 ∈ W_G and (2) says that the F-rank of G_0 equals the R-rank of G_0 ⊗ R, namely n for C_n (then G_0 is split), 2 for SO(m, 2) and ⌊n/2⌋ for SO^*(2n); for type A_n, (2) says G_0 is the adjoint group of a unitary group of a hermitian form over a CM quadratic extension of F (not an inner form of one); n = 1 covers Hilbert modular varieties.
items.note: Corrected: the printed paragraph says G^ad_R is split for types B, C, D_n (n even), which holds only for type C (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: Prasad–Rapinchuk: forms with prescribed real form and maximal Q-rank
items.statement: Let G_0 be a quasi-split absolutely simple Q-group and G_R an inner form of G_{0,R}. There is an inner form G of G_0 over Q with G ⊗ R ≅ G_R (as inner forms of G_{0,R}) whose Q-rank equals the R-rank of G_R.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 3.3.10, p. 33, citing [PR06, Thm 1]
items.note: The printed proof says 'the R-rank of G_{0,R}' where the parenthetical note shows G_R is meant (sourceIssues E10).

items.name: Corollary 3.3.10: existence of Shimura data satisfying 3.3.5
items.statement: For every irreducible Hermitian symmetric domain X and every imaginary quadratic field L there is a Shimura datum (G, X) with G absolutely simple, split over L, satisfying condition 3.3.5.

items.name: The boundary torus torsor ξ_K → C_K
items.statement: Under 3.3.5, let P ∈ [P_Σ̃] be defined over Q with unipotent radical U and centre Z, U(Z) = U(Q) ∩ K, Z(Z) = Z(Q) ∩ K; ξ_K = U(Z)\U(R)Z(C) and C_K = (Z(C)/Z(Z))\ξ_K. Then C_K is an abelian variety and ξ_K → C_K a torsor under the torus Z(C)/Z(Z); for a smooth fan Σ in X_*(Z(C)/Z(Z))_Q (a cone decomposition of the positive cone) one obtains a smooth torus embedding ξ_K(Σ) → C_K with normal crossings boundary D_K(Σ). For P_Σ̃ the relevant boundary Shimura variety is zero-dimensional.
items.note: The printed text places the fan in X^*(…) (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.13(1): the boundary neighbourhood has the torsor's fundamental group
items.statement: There is an analytic neighbourhood V_K of D_K(Σ) in ξ_K(Σ)(C) with V_K^* = V_K ∖ D_K(Σ) = U(Z)\X^+ ⊂ ξ_K(C) such that V_K^* → ξ_K(C) induces an isomorphism of topological fundamental groups (both ≅ U(Z)).

items.name: Proposition 3.3.13(2): the étale chart of the toroidal compactification
items.statement: There are an ncd compactification Sh_K(Σ)^+ of Sh_K^+ and an étale map of complex analytic spaces π_K : V_K → Sh_K(Σ)^+ with π_K^{-1}(Sh_K(Σ)^+ ∖ Sh_K^+) = D_K(Σ), such that π_K : V_K^* → Sh_K^+ induces the inclusion U(Z) ↪ Γ on fundamental groups.

items.name: ncd compactification
items.statement: For a smooth C-scheme Y, an ncd compactification is a dense open embedding Y ⊂ Ȳ into a proper smooth C-scheme with Ȳ ∖ Y a normal crossings divisor.

items.name: Connected components of Shimura varieties
items.statement: For a connected component X^+ ⊂ X, the corresponding component of Sh_K is Sh_K^+ = Γ\X^+ with Γ = K ∩ G(Q)_+, G(Q)_+ the elements mapping to the identity component of G^ad(R); for neat K its fundamental group is Γ.

items.name: Parabolics extend to reductive models
items.statement: If G has a reductive model G_{Z_p}, a parabolic P ⊂ G_{Q_p} extends to a parabolic P_{Z_p} ⊂ G_{Z_p} because the scheme of parabolic subgroups is projective ([SGA3, XXVI Cor. 3.5]); P_{Z_p} is attached to a cocharacter in [μ_Σ̃] defined over Z_p.
items.note: Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 8 includes the relative theory over a base.

items.name: Lemma 3.3.15: the integral unipotent radical is a pro-p Heisenberg extension
items.statement: U_{Z_p}(Z_p) is a central extension of finitely generated free abelian pro-p groups; U(Z_p) → U(F_p) is surjective; and U(F_p) is a mod p reduction of U(Z_p) (a finite Heisenberg group, via the F_p^×-action through μ_{Z_p} with weights 1 and 2).

items.name: Strong approximation for unipotent groups
items.statement: For a unipotent Q-group U and a compact open K, U(Q) is dense in U(A_f); in particular the closure of U(Z) = U(Q) ∩ K in U(Z_p) is U(Z_p), and the pro-p completion of U(Z) is U(Z_p).
items.note: AA.4 plans strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple groups only; ShimuraVarieties V0 restricts its use to semisimple simply connected groups.

items.name: Principal p-congruence cover
items.statement: With K = K_pK^p, K_p = G(Z_p) for a reductive model G_{Z_p}, K^1_p = ker(G(Z_p) → G(F_p)), K^1 = K^1_pK^p, Γ = K ∩ G(Q)_+ and Γ_1 = K^1 ∩ G(Q)_+, the covering Γ_1\X^+ → Γ\X^+ is a principal p-covering.

items.name: Algebraic versus analytic p-essential dimension at the boundary
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 3.3.17 the pullback along π_K of Γ_1\X^+ → Γ\X^+ has a component V^*_{K^1} → V^*_K which is the restriction of the U(F_p)-covering of schemes ξ_{K^1} → ξ_K; with V_{K^1} = ξ_{K^1}(Σ)^an|_{V_K}, and since π_K^{-1} of the Zariski closure of a Zariski closed B ⊂ Sh_K^+ is Zariski closed in V_K, ed(Γ_1\X^+ → Γ\X^+; p) ≥ ed(V_{K^1} → V_K; p).

items.name: Theorem 3.3.17: incompressibility of principal p-coverings
items.statement: Assume condition 3.3.5 and that G extends to a reductive group scheme over Z_p. If Σ ≠ c(Σ) assume p > dim X + (dim Z + 1)/2, p > dim X + 2, and that p is a prime of unramified good reduction for ξ_K. Then ed(Γ_1\X^+ → Γ\X^+; p) = dim X.
items.note: Corrected statement: p > dim X + 2 is added (sourceIssues E14); the proof applies Proposition 3.2.14 and Corollary 3.2.17 to the non-proper torus embedding ξ_K(Σ) → C_K (sourceIssues E16).

items.name: Good reduction of boundary torus torsors for Hodge-type data
items.statement: If (G, X) is of Hodge type and G extends to a reductive group over Z_p (K_p hyperspecial), then the boundary torus torsor ξ_K → C_K of 3.3.11, and its torus embeddings ξ_K(Σ), have unramified good reduction at p, via the integral toroidal compactifications of Madapusi Pera.
items.note: ShimuraCompactifications C5 builds integral compactifications for PEL data only and states that it makes no claim for Hodge- or abelian-type data.

items.name: Corollary 3.3.18: the Hodge-type case
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 3.3.17 with (G, X) of Hodge type, p is a prime of unramified good reduction for ξ_K, and the conclusion of Theorem 3.3.17 holds without that assumption.

items.name: Classical Hermitian types are of abelian type
items.statement: An adjoint Shimura datum (G, X) whose Hermitian domain is of classical type (A, B, C, D^R, and D^H in the cases of [Del79, 2.3.10]) is of abelian type: there is a Hodge-type datum (G', X') with a central isogeny G'^der → G^der inducing an isomorphism of adjoint data.

items.name: Hodge-type lifts with reductive models over Z_p
items.statement: If (G, X) is of abelian type and G has a reductive model over Z_p, the Hodge-type datum (G', X') of the previous item can be chosen so that G' also has a reductive model over Z_p.

items.name: Principal p-coverings under central isogeny
items.statement: For a central isogeny G' → G as above with reductive models over Z_p, the map Γ'_1\Γ' → Γ_1\Γ of principal p-covering groups has kernel and cokernel finite of order prime to p, and p-essential dimension is unchanged under such a change of covering group.

items.name: Corollary 3.3.19: existence of p-incompressible congruence covers
items.statement: Let X be an irreducible Hermitian symmetric domain and L/Q an imaginary quadratic field. There is a Shimura datum (G, X) with G absolutely simple and split over L such that every principal p-covering Γ_1\X^+ → Γ\X^+ satisfies ed = dim X, provided, when X is not a tube domain: for X of classical type, p > (3/2) dim X and p > dim X + 2 (the proof uses dim X = (dim U + dim Z)/2 and dim X + (dim Z + 1)/2 ≤ (3/2) dim X); for type E_6, p sufficiently large.
items.note: Corrected: the printed corollary allows any quadratic L (sourceIssues E9) and omits p > dim X + 2 (E14).
